about: Feels Bad Man is a simple cartoon of Pepe the Frog in a blue shirt, drawn from the shoulders up with heavy drooping eyelids, watery glossy eyes and a big brown lower lip pushed into a pout. It is a pure image of quiet, self-pitying disappointment. The caption "feels bad man" became internet shorthand for small personal letdowns: a canceled plan, a lost save file, a long-awaited sequel turning out mediocre. It is the gloomy counterpart to the smug, happy "feels good man" version of the same frog, and it works best for relatable, low-stakes sadness rather than real tragedy.
origin: Pepe the Frog was created by artist Matt Furie for his comic Boy's Club in the mid-2000s. The sad version and the "feels bad man" line grew on 4chan in the late 2000s as a mirror of the original "feels good man" Pepe.
usage:
The top box describes the small disappointment, usually in a flat, first-person way, like "wake up excited for the weekend" or "finally get to the front of the line". The bottom box is the payoff: either the classic "feels bad man" or the twist that ruins it.

Keep the setup understated and specific; the sadness should feel petty and relatable. It also works as a pure reaction image with the top box empty and only "feels bad man" at the bottom.
ideas: finally get to the front of the line
